definition: Crude slang for the penis, dominant in Chilean vernacular and common across Peru, Bolivia, and parts of Central America.
notes: The default crude penis word in Chile; also used in Peru and Bolivia; less common in Mexico and largely unknown in Spain.

definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis.
notes: Primarily Argentina and Uruguay; 'Pirulo' is also the brand name of a popular ice cream bar in the region, generating persistent double entendres.

definition: Iberian Spanish slang for the penis, derived from the black poplar tree (chopo), whose tall, columnar form evokes a phallus.
notes: Primarily Spain; the black poplar is known for its straight, upright growth habit; limited penetration in Latin America.

definition: Slang for the penis using the word for 'log' or 'trunk,' implying substantial size and rigidity.
notes: Used across Spain and Latin America; implies a thick or large member; 'tronco' also means 'mate/buddy' in colloquial Spanish, occasionally producing ambiguity.

definition: Slang for the penis derived from 'mallet' or 'sledgehammer,' emphasizing forceful size.
notes: Primarily Iberian Spanish; the mallet metaphor foregrounds force and heft rather than length; less common than tronco across Latin America.

definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'walking stick' or 'cane,' playing on upright phallic shape.
notes: A mild, humorous metaphor used across Spanish-speaking regions; lower vulgarity than direct penis slang.

definition: English loanword adopted into Spanish as humorous slang for the penis, referencing the handheld video-game controller.
notes: Peak usage late 1990s–early 2000s, aligned with the rise of home gaming; still recognized but less actively used; same metaphor exists in English.

definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'cucumber,' a widespread vegetable-shape metaphor.
notes: One of the most widespread penis euphemisms in Spanish; the cucumber metaphor appears across many languages; 'no importar un pepino' (not to care a cucumber) adds ironic layering in Spain.

definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'carrot,' referencing its elongated tapered shape.
notes: More playful than crude; less common than pepino as a penis metaphor in Spanish; the carrot's color and taper evoke the circumcised glans.

definition: Slang for the penis using the word for 'bone,' playing on both structural hardness and the English cognate 'boner' for erection.
notes: The bone-erection metaphor works cross-linguistically; can specifically connote erection rather than the flaccid organ; used across Latin America and Spain.

definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'tool,' one of the most universal phallic metaphors across human languages.
notes: Maps directly to the English slang 'tool'; among the mildest and most socially acceptable penis euphemisms in Spanish; widely used in humorous contexts.

definition: Mild euphemism for the penis using the word for 'apparatus' or 'device,' used in quasi-clinical and humorous registers.
notes: One of the most demure penis references in Spanish; also appears in clinical contexts as 'aparato reproductor' (reproductive system), lending it a veneer of respectability even in crude usage.

definition: Mexican slang for the penis derived from 'pirinola,' a traditional wooden spinning top with a tapered, pointed tip.
notes: Primarily Mexican Spanish; the pirinola's pointed spinning tip and the act of spinning map onto penetrative connotations; limited recognition outside Mexico.

definition: Crude slang for the penis, literally 'beak' or 'tip'; among the most taboo penis terms in Chile, approaching the vulgarity ceiling of Chilean profanity.
notes: In Chile, 'pico' rivals 'pichula' in vulgarity and is censored on broadcast television; also used in Colombia and Peru; 'al pico' functions as a strong dismissive expletive in Chilean Spanish.

definition: Mexican and Central American slang for the penis, sometimes carrying connotations of thickness or large size.
notes: Primarily Mexico and Central America; in non-sexual registers 'choncho' can mean 'fat' or 'chubby,' which transfers into the size implication in sexual use.

definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis; literally 'Turk,' likely originating from ethnic stereotypes about Levantine immigrants in Argentina.
notes: Primarily Argentina; Argentina received substantial Levantine Arab immigration in the 19th–20th centuries, colloquially called 'turcos'; the ethnic attribution of sexual prowess to this group appears to underlie the slang.

definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis; literally a squat clay jug or earthenware pot, metaphorically referencing genital shape.
notes: Primarily Argentina and Uruguay; in Uruguay 'botija' separately means 'kid' or 'boy' in everyday slang, adding double-meaning potential; low recognition outside the River Plate region.

definition: Augmentative of 'polla' (the dominant Iberian Spanish crude term for penis), meaning a large penis; the '-ón' suffix marks exceptional size.
notes: Derived from 'polla' + augmentative '-ón'; primarily Iberian Spanish where 'polla' is the default vulgar penis word; register and tone parallel English 'big dick.'

definition: Spanish slang for the glans penis; literally 'cocoon' or 'flower bud,' evoking the rounded tip of the penis; simultaneously a high-frequency general insult in Spain.
notes: Has dual currency in Spain: anatomically specific (glans) and as a general-purpose insult roughly equivalent to British 'bellend' or 'knob'; both meanings are simultaneously active; less common in Latin America.

definition: The clinical term for the internal muscular canal extending from the cervix to the vulvar vestibule; the standard anatomical term in Spanish medical and educational contexts.
notes: Identical spelling to the English clinical term; Latin origin; frequently misapplied by lay speakers to denote the external genitalia (vulva) as well.

definition: The clinical term for the external female genitalia, encompassing the labia majora and minora, clitoris, and vaginal opening.
notes: Identical to the English clinical term; significantly underrecognized by the general population relative to 'vagina,' despite being the visible external anatomy; recognition has risen with sex-education campaigns.

definition: The clinical Spanish term for the vaginal lips (labia), used generically to cover both the labia majora and labia minora.
notes: Generic clinical term; the more precise distinction is 'labios mayores' (labia majora) and 'labios menores' (labia minora); 'labios vaginales' is preferred in sex-education contexts for accessibility.

definition: The clinical Spanish term for the vaginal introitus — the external entrance to the vaginal canal.
notes: Highly specialized medical terminology; rarely encountered outside gynecological or anatomical discourse; the full form 'introito vaginal' is more common in clinical writing than the standalone noun.

definition: The clinical and literary Spanish term for the mons pubis — the rounded fatty prominence over the pubic symphysis; literally 'Mount of Venus.'
notes: Translates Latin 'mons Veneris'; bridges clinical anatomy and literary tradition via the mythological reference to Venus; known to educated speakers but not universally recognized.

definition: The clinical Spanish term specifically denoting the internal muscular channel of the vagina from the cervix to the vaginal opening.
notes: More anatomically precise than 'vagina' alone, emphasizing the tubular structure; common in obstetric contexts (e.g., 'parto por canal vaginal' = vaginal delivery).
